items.title: Dinguiraye : un élève de 8 ans meurt noyé dans une fosse septique, à Fougah
items.description: Un drame s’est produit ce mardi 11 août 2026 dans le secteur de Fougah, à Dinguiraye. Mohamed Camara, un élève âgé de 8 ans, a perdu la vie après être tombé dans une fosse septique alors qu’il était parti se baigner avec des camarades. Selon les informations recueillies auprès de ses proches, Mohamed Camara s’était rendu sur les lieux avec plusieurs enfants de son âge pour se baigner. C’est au cours de cette activité qu’il serait tombé dans une fosse septique remplie d’eau. Mohamed Hady Tall, oncle et tuteur du défunt, raconte les circonstances dans lesquelles il a appris la nouvelle. « C'est mon neveu. J'étais à mon domicile lorsque les enfants avec lesquels il s'amusait sont venus me dire que Mohamed est tombé dans une fosse septique. Je suis immédiatement sorti en criant : au secours, au secours, mon neveu est tombé dans une fosse septique ». Alerté par les enfants, Mohamed Hady Tall s'est précipité vers le lieu de l'accident. À son arrivée, un voisin avait déjà commencé à intervenir pour tenter de sauver l'enfant. « Avant mon arrivée sur les lieux, il y a un de mes voisins qui était déjà sur place. Il est descendu dans la fosse pour sauver l'enfant », témoigne-t-il. Malgré cette intervention, les tentatives de secours n'ont pas permis de sauver Mohamed Camara. Son oncle explique avoir lui-même tenté de le réanimer après l’extraction de son neveu de la fosse. « À mon arrivée, j'ai essayé de le réanimer avec le bouche à bouche mais il était déjà décédé », déplore Mohamed Hady Tall. Le défunt, Mohamed Camara, était âgé de seulement 8 ans et fréquentait l'école. Il était élève en classe de 3 ᵉ année, selon son oncle et tuteur. Ce nouveau drame rappelle les risques auxquels peuvent être exposés les enfants en cette saison pluvieuse avec les fosses septiques ou d'autres points d'eau non sécurisés. items.title: Court turns down bail for alleged romance scam pastor
items.description: An Accra Circuit Court has for the second time remanded an online pastor into police custody over alleged romance scams involving seven complainants. Nana Yaw Bonsu Kwarteng, 35, an entrepreneur, is jointly charged with his wife, Sally Akosua Amoasah, a chartered accountant, with six counts of conspiracy to commit crime, namely defrauding by false pretences. Inspector Frank Morgan Dorvi, leading the prosecution, opposed bail for Kwarteng, saying he was a flight risk and investigations were ongoing. Kwarteng faces additional charges of defrauding by false pretences, resisting arrest, and making, producing and possessing obscene material, while Sally faces an additional charge of making, producing and possessing obscene material. The couple has denied the charges. The court granted Sally bail in the sum of GH¢100,000 with two sureties and ordered her to report to the case investigator every Monday and Friday. Inspector Dorvi told the court that Kwarteng was a flight risk and that the Police had information that he possessed an international passport that could enable him to leave the jurisdiction if granted bail. He said, in the interest of fairness, the Police were ready for an expeditious trial. The prosecutor told the court that one of the complainants was incurring substantial hotel and accommodation bills. Defence counsel, Mr Yaw Danquah, disputed the prosecution’s assertions, saying his client was not a flight risk and should be admitted to bail. Mr Danquah said Kwarteng’s Ghanaian passport was with the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). He said the allegations against Kwarteng were not supported by evidence and that the prosecution’s submissions amounted to an attack on his client’s character. Mr Danquah also argued that Sally had not committed any crime and questioned her prosecution over an allegation that she received a nude picture from her husband. The amended facts before the court stated that the seven complainants included an ambassador and businesswomen. The prosecution said Kwarteng operated an Instagram page, Nana Bonsu Kwarteng, with about 21,000 followers, on which he presented himself as a pastor. It said Sally participated in Kwarteng’s online services by sharing scripture verses on the screen and reading the Bible. The prosecution said that in October 2024, Kwarteng contacted the first complainant, who was also a follower on Instagram, and proposed that they become friends. It said Kwarteng later told the woman that God had revealed to him that she was his wife and promised to marry her. The prosecution said he visited her family in Nigeria and later told her that he was engaged in a lucrative car tyre business. It said Kwarteng subsequently demanded and collected $33,000 from her to clear a container of tyres that was incurring demurrage. The prosecution said he assured the woman that he would repay the money, knowing that she had borrowed it from a business associate. It said when the repayment became due, Kwarteng allegedly began avoiding her and threatened to share and publish her nude videos. The prosecution said Kwarteng shared the woman’s nude videos with Sally. The court heard that Kwarteng used a similar approach with the second complainant, whom he met through his online platform and later proposed to marry after visiting her family. The prosecution said he collected GH¢25,000 from the second complainant to clear car tyres, with an undertaking to repay the money after the transaction, but allegedly failed to do so and subsequently avoided her. It said Kwarteng used similar methods in his dealings with the third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh complainants, including proposing marriage and visiting their families. The prosecution also alleged that during the relationships, Kwarteng intentionally captured intimate photographs and videos of some of the complainants without their knowledge. It said he demanded and collected $4,000, GH¢22,000 and other foreign currencies from other complainants. The prosecution said after Kwarteng and Sally realised that the complainants were pursuing them, Kwarteng deactivated his Instagram page while Sally changed hers. It said the two accused persons went into hiding after they were wanted by the Police and EOCO. The prosecution said Kwarteng failed to honour repeated police invitations to assist with investigations. It said on July 18, 2026, Kwarteng and Sally used part of the money allegedly collected from the complainants to celebrate their marriage ceremony in Kumasi. The prosecution said intelligence led to their arrest at a hideout on July 20, 2026, adding that Kwarteng attempted to escape but was recaptured. It said investigations established that Sally registered a sole proprietorship company in her name, which was allegedly used to give the complainants the impression that the accused persons operated a legitimate business. The prosecution also alleged that investigations uncovered several sexual recordings which Kwarteng had secretly made involving different women and allegedly used to threaten or blackmail them when they demanded refunds. It said Kwarteng was also the subject of other similar cases before EOCO and the Nima Police, while investigations indicated that other persons had allegedly fallen prey to the alleged romance scam since 2021. The prosecution said additional persons had contacted the Police claiming to have been affected by Kwarteng’s activities, while other women had petitioned the Inspector-General of Police over the matter. It said investigations were ongoing.

items.title: Asokwa MCE links recent MoMo vendor attacks to Asafo Market decongestion
items.description: The Municipal Chief Executive for Asokwa, Amoh Kamel, has linked recent attacks on Mobile Money (MoMo) vendors in parts of the municipality to the decongestion exercise carried out around the Asafo Market by the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA). According to him, the exercise displaced groups of people from the Asafo Market area, some of whom subsequently moved into communities across Greater Kumasi. He said the movement may have contributed to isolated security incidents in neighbouring municipalities, including attacks on MoMo vendors at Kaase and Ahensan Estate. Mr Kamel made the comments while speaking to the media on Tuesday, August 11, during an exhibition showcasing the newly transformed Assembly Hall of the Asokwa Municipal Assembly. He said the security concerns had prompted the Municipal Security Council (MUSEC) to hold a series of emergency meetings and introduce measures to strengthen security across the municipality. “As the head of municipal security, I have stepped up security operations and police patrols across the municipality,” he said. The MCE assured residents and business owners that additional security had been deployed to vulnerable areas and urged them to continue their activities without fear. His comments follow the arrest of two suspects believed to be connected to the recent attacks on MoMo vendors. Mr Kamel said the suspects were arrested by the Ashanti Regional Police Command’s Anti-Robbery Team, with support from the municipal and divisional police commands, through intelligence-led operations. “Our prime suspects were arrested yesterday by the regional anti-robbery team with the support of our municipal and divisional police commanders,” he said. He added that the municipality was awaiting an official briefing from the Ashanti Regional Police Command. “I can confirm that the two key suspects behind these incidents are in custody,” he said.

items.title: Osun people’ll vote for me to end thuggery, restore peace — ADC’s Salaam
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The African Democratic Congress governorship candidate in Osun State, Najeem Salaam, has expressed confidence that voters will back him in Saturday’s election, saying his track record makes him the candidate best placed to end political thuggery and restore peace in the state Speaking at Arise News’ Town Hall ahead of the election, Salaam said Osun residents were tired of political violence and would support the candidate and party they believed could guarantee peace. “Osun people do not want thuggery again because they see us and study as the most peaceful party. They also know the only candidate that can bring peace is Najeem Salam and the only party that can bring peace is the ADC,” he said. The former lawmaker alleged that political violence and the proliferation of weapons remained major concerns in the state, warning that choosing other candidates could worsen existing tensions. “Osun people know that if they give it to A or B, they will fight. I can tell you that Osun is filled with thuggery and ammunition. So, we will bring peace,” Salaam said. He said his ambition was to build a better future for Osun residents through good governance, human development and policies targeted at improving the lives of the people. “To build a better today and tomorrow for Osun. I go in to develop Osun in a better way, give people what belongs to them. I am more than fit than any other governor,” he said. Salaam also described himself as a reserved politician who relies on research and planning, saying the policies contained in his 10-point agenda were realistic and achievable. “I am a very reserved person. I conduct research and all that constitute them in my ten-point agenda are doable. It is codified for people that would have access to it. I have been in government and I know how we did,” he said. The ADC candidate further highlighted his grassroots political experience, saying he began his political career at the local government level and had spent years engaging with communities and understanding their needs. “I started my political career from the local government. I have been looking after people and I know their needs. If I have the opportunity, I will serve humanity,” Salaam said. He said his experience in government, grassroots engagement and policy agenda had prepared him to lead Osun, adding that restoring peace would be a major priority of his administration if elected. items.title: Profession d'avocat : La Cour constitutionnelle refuse de statuer en l’état
items.description: La Cour constitutionnelle a refusé, en l’état, de se prononcer sur la conformité à la Constitution de la loi n° 66.23 relative à l’organisation de la profession d’avocat, estimant que les conditions juridiques nécessaires à l’examen du texte n’étaient pas réunies. Dans une décision dont Hespress FR a obtenu copie, l’institution a déclaré l’impossibilité de statuer sur la saisine qui lui a été transmise, tout en ordonnant la notification de son arrêt au Chef du gouvernement, au président de la Chambre des représentants et au président de la Chambre des conseillers, ainsi que sa publication au Bulletin officiel. Au cœur de cette décision figure une question de procédure. La Cour relève que la lettre de saisine émanant du président de la Chambre des représentants, bien qu’ayant pour objet le contrôle de constitutionnalité de la loi n° 66.23, était accompagnée d’un dossier ne contenant pas le texte définitif de la loi tel qu’adopté par le Parlement. Selon la juridiction, le document transmis consistait principalement en une copie du rapport de la Commission de la justice, de la législation et des droits de l’Homme de la Chambre des conseillers établi dans le cadre d’une deuxième lecture du projet de loi. Ce rapport comprenait plusieurs pièces, notamment le texte du projet tel qu’approuvé par la Chambre des représentants lors de sa deuxième lecture du 6 juillet 2026. En revanche, il ne contenait pas la version du texte adoptée par la Chambre des conseillers lors de sa propre deuxième lecture, le 7 juillet 2026. Cette absence est apparue déterminante aux yeux de la Cour constitutionnelle. Celle-ci rappelle que le troisième alinéa de l’article 132 de la Constitution autorise le Roi, le Chef du gouvernement, le président de la Chambre des représentants, le président de la Chambre des conseillers, un cinquième des membres de la Chambre des représentants ou quarante membres de la Chambre des conseillers à saisir la juridiction constitutionnelle avant la promulgation d’une loi afin qu’elle se prononce sur sa conformité à la Loi fondamentale. La Cour souligne également que l’article 23 de sa loi organique encadre précisément cette procédure. Ce texte prévoit que la saisine doit être effectuée par lettre émanant de l’une des autorités habilitées ou, le cas échéant, par une ou plusieurs lettres réunissant le nombre de signatures parlementaires requis. Une compétence limitée aux lois définitivement adoptées Dans son raisonnement, la Cour insiste sur le fait que les dispositions de la Constitution et de la loi organique doivent être interprétées de manière complémentaire. Il en ressort que son contrôle, dans le cadre du mécanisme prévu à l’article 132, ne peut s’exercer que sur des lois définitivement approuvées et régulièrement déférées à son examen. Autrement dit, la juridiction constitutionnelle ne contrôle ni les rapports des commissions parlementaires ni les projets de loi en cours d’élaboration. Son intervention ne peut porter que sur un texte législatif adopté et formellement transmis selon les règles prévues par le droit constitutionnel marocain. La Cour considère ainsi que le constituant a instauré un lien indissociable entre l’acte de saisine et le texte soumis au contrôle. Dès lors, le simple fait d’annexer à la demande un rapport relatif aux travaux préparatoires d’une commission parlementaire, même lorsqu’il contient une version du projet de loi, ne saurait tenir lieu de transmission du texte législatif dont la constitutionnalité est contestée. Pour les juges constitutionnels, cette situation empêche matériellement l’exercice du contrôle demandé. La décision précise en effet que la Cour ne peut statuer que dans les limites fixées par la Constitution, conformément aux procédures de fond et de forme définies par sa loi organique et sur la base des documents effectivement transmis par l’autorité saisissante. L’absence d’une copie conforme du texte de loi devant faire l’objet du contrôle a donc eu une conséquence directe : elle a privé la Cour de l’objet même de son examen. Dans ces conditions, la juridiction estime que le support juridique nécessaire à son intervention n’existe pas en l’état, ce qui constitue un obstacle légal à toute décision sur le fond. En conséquence, la Cour constitutionnelle a conclu qu’elle ne pouvait se prononcer sur la constitutionnalité d’un texte qui ne lui a pas été soumis conformément aux exigences fixées par la Constitution et par la loi organique régissant son fonctionnement. Elle a ainsi déclaré qu’il lui était impossible, dans les circonstances actuelles, de statuer sur la saisine relative à la loi n° 66.23 portant organisation de la profession d’avocat. The post Profession d'avocat : La Cour constitutionnelle refuse de statuer en l’état appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: The Atlantic Festival announces interview with Colin Kaepernick and exclusive preview of Netflix’s East of Eden, with Florence Pugh, Zoe Kazan, and Bela Bajaria

The festival will also feature an exclusive first look of Netflix’s limited series East of Eden , a fresh interpretation of John Steinbeck's novel that has been adapted and executive produced by Zoe Kazan , who also serves as co-showrunner. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Kazan, the series’ executive producer and star Florence Pugh , and Bela Bajaria , the chief content officer of Netflix, moderated by staff writer Shirley Li . Also at The Atlantic Festival: Pete Buttigieg ; Andrew Card and Karl Rove ; Rahm Emanuel ; Bumble’s Whitney Wolfe Herd ; Representative Chip Roy ; Olympian Ibtihaj Muhammad ; San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria , Fort Worth Mayor Mattie Parker , and Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval ; University of California President James B. Milliken , Mount Holyoke College President Danielle R. Holley , and Columbia University President Jennifer L. items.title: Galamsey has polluted 60% of Ghana’s water bodies — CSIR-WRI scientist
items.description: About 60 per cent of Ghana’s water bodies are polluted, a senior scientist at the CSIR-Water Research Institute (CSIR-WRI), Dr Franco Enobrenaco, has warned. Dr Enobrenaco, of the Groundwater and Geoscience Division, said the situation was largely driven by illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, which continues to contaminate the country’s rivers and groundwater. He warned that the remaining 40 per cent of relatively unpolluted water bodies could also come under threat as the population grows and mining activities continue. Speaking during a presentation at the CSIR-WRI Mid-Year Review 2026 on the theme, *“Can Ghana Heal Her Waters? Toward Sustainable Remediation of Polluted Water Bodies,”* he cautioned that Ghana could eventually be forced to import water if urgent measures were not taken to protect its water resources. “If we have 100% and 60% of our water bodies polluted, the rest is 40%… We are going to import water. I know that some people are already importing water,” he said. Dr Enobrenaco called for a two-pronged approach involving the reduction or elimination of illegal mining, the provision of alternative livelihoods for affected miners and strict enforcement of mining laws. He said efforts to restore polluted water bodies would remain ineffective if the sources of pollution were not addressed. He also urged authorities to adopt integrated remediation methods rather than relying on a single technology. According to him, polluted water poses serious risks to public health, agriculture, industry and energy generation, while treating contaminated water also comes at a significant economic cost. Citing the restoration of the Thames River in the United Kingdom as evidence that polluted water bodies can be recovered, he said Ghana could restore its rivers through sustained, coordinated action involving government, researchers, communities and other stakeholders.

items.title: Criminal trials during legal vacations a ‘novel’ departure from tradition — Kpemka
items.description: A former Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Joseph Kpemka, has described as “novel” the decision by specialised High Courts to continue substantive criminal trials during Ghana’s ongoing legal vacation. His comments follow the Accra High Court’s rejection of an application by lawyers for four accused persons, including former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive Officer Dr Mustapha Abdul-Hamid, seeking to adjourn proceedings until October. The development has sparked debate within the legal profession because the traditional practice during the legal vacation has been for designated Vacation Courts to focus mainly on urgent applications, motions and interlocutory matters. According to Mr Kpemka, substantive hearings have generally not formed part of the work of courts sitting during the vacation. “During the holidays, judges do not normally deal with the substantive hearings. It is only motions. The holiday judges sit to hear motions and urgent applications,” he said, stressing that the decision to continue full criminal trials represented a departure from the usual practice. “It is novel. We’ve not done that,” he added. The Abdul-Hamid case is among several high-profile criminal matters designated to continue during the legal vacation. The decision comes amid a wider debate over the scope and purpose of the legal vacation, following a recent appeal by the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) to Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie for judges to respect established practices governing the period.

items.title: ¿Dónde habrá nubes durante el eclipse? Consulte cómo estarán los cielos y el horizonte en cada municipio
items.description: Las nubes bajas pueden convertirse en el peor enemigo de alguien que quiera ver el eclipse de este 12 de agosto. En el siguiente mapa mostramos dos modelos que estiman la nubosidad prevista para las 20 horas del miércoles en cada municipio y hacia el horizonte, además del detalle de altura de las nubes. La última previsión disponible se actualizó la mañana de este martes e incorpora los datos horarios de AEMET, de alta resolución. Seguir leyendo Metodología del mapa El mapa muestra una previsión de nubosidad para la hora del eclipse en cada punto de España. La capa visible representa la nubosidad total prevista por el modelo del Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo (ECMWF), distribuido por AEMET a través de CEPPM. Su resolución aproximada es de 5 kilómetros. Dese el martes, el mapa incorporará también HARMONIE-AROME, el modelo de alta resolución de AEMET. Su rejilla, de aproximadamente 2,5 kilómetros, permite consultar la nubosidad prevista por horas concretas con más detalle local que el modelo europeo de medio plazo. Las fichas de cada lugar combinan dos tipos de información. Por un lado la nubosidad total prevista en ese punto por CEPPM, expresada en intervalos de porcentaje; y por otro la estructura vertical media de las nubes en el municipio según AIFS , el modelo de inteligencia artificial del ECMWF, con una resolución aproximada de 25 kilómetros (distingue entre nubes bajas, medias y altas) La clasificación de las condiciones —favorable, regular o desfavorable— combina la nubosidad total del punto con la proporción de nubes bajas, medias y altas prevista sobre el municipio. El cálculo da más peso a las nubes bajas, un peso intermedio a las medias y menor a las altas. La ficha municipal no suma las tres capas de AIFS: las nubes bajas, medias y altas pueden coexistir a distintas alturas. Se muestran como una descripción de la estructura vertical prevista, no como partes excluyentes de un mismo 100%. El modo “Vista al horizonte” es una estimación complementaria. Calcula la dirección y altura del Sol en el máximo local del eclipse y toma tres muestras de nube baja AIFS en la línea de visión, a alturas aproximadas de entre 1 y 2 kilómetros. Muestra el escenario más nuboso de esas muestras. Es una orientación sobre posibles nubes entre el observador y el Sol, no una predicción detallada del relieve ni de la visibilidad exacta.

items.title: Nana B begins campaign tour in Ashanti region as he eyes NPP 1st Vice chair position
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Organiser, Henry Nana Boakye, has officially begun his campaign for the position of National 1st Vice Chair, starting with engagements across the Ashanti Region. Mr Boakye said he chose the Ashanti Region as the starting point because of its historical importance to the NPP and his personal connection to the region. He said he met with delegates from 12 constituencies as part of efforts to present his vision and seek their support ahead of the party’s internal election. Mr Boakye also engaged members of the party’s Regional Communications team, television and radio callers, as well as social media team members, acknowledging their contribution towards defending and promoting the NPP’s interests. He described the groups as individuals who work daily to communicate the party’s message on various platforms. Mr Boakye said the engagements had left him encouraged by what he described as the determination of party members to rebuild the NPP and return it to political power. “The journey to re-organise, to re-energise, and to lead the NPP to more victories begins now, and it begins at home,” he said. He expressed gratitude to party members for the reception and support during his engagements, saying the Ashanti Region had made its position clear on the need for a stronger and more organised NPP ahead of the party’s next electoral contest.

items.title: CDD-Ghana calls for investigations into unresolved 2020 and 2024 election violence cases
items.description: The Ghana Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) has called for investigations into unresolved cases of electoral violence recorded during Ghana’s 2020 and 2024 general elections, arguing that the country cannot achieve lasting peace without justice for victims and accountability for perpetrators. Speaking to the media at an inter-party dialogue organised by the National Peace Council in Accra, CDD-Ghana Programmes Manager for Security Sector Governance and Local and Urban Governance, Paul Kwabena Aborampah, said families affected by electoral violence continue to live with the pain and trauma of losing their loved ones. He warned that memories of the incidents are often revived during subsequent election periods, creating the risk of retaliation. “You can’t have peace without justice, and people whose relatives have been affected are still in the system. They probably know people who committed the crime, so anytime there are elections, it seems to ginger them to retaliate,” he said. Lessons from National Reconciliation Mr Aborampah cited Ghana’s post-military regime national reconciliation process as an example of how allowing victims to tell their stories can contribute to healing, even where financial compensation is not provided. “As Ghana had national reconciliation post-military regime era, people were not compensated but having opportunity to tell their story, they were satisfied. So we believe conducting these investigations and bringing the perpetrators to book, even if we don’t extract any compensation for the family, they will be okay telling their stories,” he said. Background on Electoral Violence The call comes amid ongoing efforts to address the troubling trend of electoral violence that has marred Ghana’s democratic process. A special investigative task force established by the Inspector General of Police identified 12 key cases of violence associated with the 2020 and 2024 general elections, which claimed 15 lives and left more than 40 people injured across seven regions. The affected regions include Greater Accra, Ashanti, Bono East, Savannah, Northern, Upper East and Upper West. The investigation found that the majority of these incidents involved the use of firearms during confrontations between supporters of opposing political parties. In some cases, security personnel resorted to live ammunition as a means of crowd control, often without proper command or adherence to engagement protocols. Interior Minister Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak has confirmed that 21 suspects have been identified in connection with the violence, with four currently on police bail, five remanded into prison custody, and arrest warrants issued for the remaining individuals. Four cases are currently before the courts, with others under investigation or at the Attorney General’s office for advice. Concerns Over Political Friction Mr Aborampah also expressed concern over what he described as unending political friction, warning that tensions are increasingly extending beyond election periods. According to him, persistent political attacks and personal criticisms risk diverting attention from national development and efforts to improve citizens’ livelihoods. “We are witnessing unending political frictions which, of course, is dangerous for us. It stalls governance, redirects attention and focus. While citizens are talking about development trajectory and peace, suggesting alternatives for the improvement of livelihoods, we will be concentrating on personal assassination, attacks and criticisms,” he added. Path Forward CDD-Ghana has indicated that investigating the unresolved cases and holding perpetrators accountable would help address grievances and strengthen public confidence in Ghana’s democratic processes. The government has already committed to compensating bereaved families and victims of the electoral violence, with the Interior Minister stating that the State would assume responsibility where conclusive evidence could not be established against any specific individual or group. The Ministry has also pledged to implement recommendations from the task force report, including improved crowd-control training for police officers, better coordination among security agencies, and sustained education for political party executives and stakeholders on the Vigilantism and Related Offences Act, 2019 (Act 999).

items.title: Re-polling set for Aug 15 at some polling stations in two Bagh constituencies of AJK
items.description: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Tuesday ordered re-polling at some polling stations in two constituencies in Poonch Division’s Bagh district. Polling in four constituencies of Bagh and Haveli districts was held on Monday as part of the third and final phase of AJK elections. Balloting in the Poonch and Sudhnoti districts had been postponed over law and order concerns in the wake of tensions between protesters and authorities. Re-polling at nine polling stations in LA-15 (Bagh Central) and 14 polling stations in LA-16 (Bagh East) will be held on August 15 (Saturday), AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal told Dawn at his office on Tuesday. Re-polling has been ordered as the electoral process at some stations either could not begin on time or was disrupted and subsequently cancelled. Of the four constituencies that went to the polls on Monday, the PPP and PML-N appear set to win one seat each, while a lesser-known party has won the third seat and the result of the fourth is awaited. According to the latest unofficial figures, PPP’s Sardar Ziaul Qamar was leading the race for LA-15 with 16,637 votes, while PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas was trailing him with 15,015 votes. Jamaat-i-Islami’s Brig (retd) Dr Mohammad Khan had secured 12,259 votes. The nine polling stations where re-polling has been ordered have 5,032 registered voters. Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party president and former AJK prime minister Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who had won the constituency in the 2021 election on a PTI ticket, appeared to be out of the race. In LA-16, PML-N’s Sardar Mir Akbar was leading PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman, who is the father of the PPP candidate in LA-15 and has served as an AJK minister in several PPP governments. Akbar had secured 19,515 votes, while Zaman had polled 16,290. The 14 stations where re-polling will be held are said to account for about 7,200 votes. Meanwhile, the Election Commission issued the preliminary results for LA-14 (Dhirkot), where Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the little-known Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party defeated Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan. Abbasi secured 40,522 votes, more than double that of Attique, who ranked second with 19,637 ballots in his favour, Form-27 showed. Form-27 lists cumulative results based on votes cast on the polling day (August 10) and by the election staff in advance polling . Abbasi contested his first election on his party’s ticket in the constituency where the Muslim Conference president, and before him his uncle and father, had been elected in all nine elections since 1985. Attique’s defeat also appeared to underscore the political decline of what was once the largest and longest-ruling party in AJK, but was reduced to a marginal force following the emergence of the PML-N in 2010. PML-N alleges tampering in AJK PM’s constituency The result of LA-17 (Haveli), from where AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore was contesting, was still awaited, while PML-N candidate Chaudhry Mohsin Aziz demanded a recount. Aziz alleged that Form-24s from different polling stations, containing the votes secured by each candidate, had been tampered with. Following this, Election Commission officials began looking into the matter, while the ballot papers were reportedly transported under tight security to Muzaffarabad for counting. Sources in the Election Commission said further decisions on the matter would be taken after the polling bags and relevant election records reached the commission’s office. In a statement, Aziz urged PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to agree to a recount in LA-17, offering to quit politics if he failed to emerge victorious by a heavy majority. Terming Rathore a “Form-47 prime minister”, Aziz said: “We possess the results signed by the presiding officers of all polling stations, showing a clear winning margin of 8,600 votes.” He claimed there was a stark difference between the results in their possession and those held by the returning officer (RO). He alleged that their application for a recount, submitted to the RO, had been rejected. “The RO’s partiality has destroyed the peaceful atmosphere of Haveli, but we will not allow anyone to steal our mandate,” he said. “In any case, a recount is my fundamental right, and our protest will continue until a recount is conducted and the mandate is restored,” he said. However, state-run Radio Pakistan , citing the Election Commission, reported that Rathore had won the LA-17 seat by defeating Aziz. Elections are being held across AJK in three division-wise phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities that have been ongoing for over two months. The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. On the other hand, the PPP has only won 10 constituencies so far. Polling in the first and second phase of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging , scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words. The PPP continued its allegations of electoral malpractices on Monday as well, while the PML-N has already expressed its confidence of having a two-thirds majority to form the government in the region. The third phase of the AJK elections was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

items.title: 2027: Kogi fixes N150m campaign signage fee for presidential candidates
items.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo ‎ ‎Kogi State Government has fixed N150 million as the official fee payable by presidential candidates for the placement of campaign billboards, posters and other promotional materials across the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The government also approved N50 million for senatorial candidates, N30 million for House of Representatives candidates and N5 million for State House of Assembly candidates. ‎ ‎The Commissioner for Information and Communications, Kingsley Fanwo, disclosed this in Lokoja after stakeholders met with operators in the signage and advertising sector. ‎ ‎The approved charges also cover campaign materials including branded T-shirts, caps and other political promotional items, as the state prepares for the 2027 elections and the October 2026 local government polls. ‎ ‎According to Fanwo, the fees are intended to regulate political advertising, enforce existing signage laws and boost the state’s internally generated revenue. ‎ ‎He said the rates were determined after a peer review of applicable charges in other states, adding that the government considered them affordable given the scale and reach of political campaigns. ‎ ‎Under the approved structure for the local government elections, chairmanship candidates are to pay N2 million, while councillorship candidates will pay N300,000 for campaign signage and related promotional materials. ‎ ‎Fanwo warned political parties and candidates against erecting billboards or displaying campaign materials without paying the prescribed fees and obtaining the necessary approvals. ‎ ‎He said offenders, including individuals or organisations found aiding or facilitating violations, would face prosecution. ‎ ‎The commissioner stressed that the regulation applied to all political parties and candidates, including those of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. ‎ ‎“In Kogi, APC is the ruling party, but that does not exempt any APC candidate from complying with the law. ‎ ‎“If you are an APC candidate and you did not pay the prescribed fee before placing your billboards or posters, we will remove them and you will be prosecuted. ‎ ‎“The government is for everybody. All political parties and candidates are hereby enjoined to adhere strictly to the regulations governing the placement of campaign materials across the state,” he said. ‎ ‎Fanwo said the Kogi State Signage and Advertisement Agency, KOSSAA, under the Ministry of Information and Communications, would coordinate the implementation and enforcement of the new campaign signage regime. ‎ ‎He assured that enforcement would be carried out fairly and without political discrimination. ‎ ‎Also speaking, the General Manager of KOSSAA, Richard Osaseyi, said the agency would commence full enforcement of the regulations from next week. ‎ ‎Osaseyi urged political parties, candidates, campaign organisations and billboard operators to register with the agency and obtain the requisite approvals before erecting or displaying campaign materials. ‎ ‎He warned that unauthorised campaign materials would be removed, while violators would face appropriate sanctions. The post 2027: Kogi fixes N150m campaign signage fee for presidential candidates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Communities applaud early gains under Damang Gold Mine Limited
items.description: Communities around the Damang Gold Mine Limited (DMGL ) in the western Region have applauded management, post takeover of the concession. Speaking at a press conference on behalf of the host communities, the Chief of the Bosomtwi Divisional Council, Nana Kwabena Amponsah IV, said the early developments represented positive indications of a more collaborative relationship between the mine and its host communities. “We have gathered today to publicly acknowledge the positive relationship that has developed between Damang Gold Mine Ltd and its host communities since the company assumed responsibility for the Damang Mine,” he said. He said the communities had historically sought stronger participation in mining-related decisions, increased employment opportunities for local people, improved infrastructure and a relationship with mining companies based on mutual respect and continuous engagement. According to him, the early experience under DGML suggested that those objectives could be pursued through dialogue and cooperation. According to the Chiefs, barely four months after Damang Gold Mine Limited (DGML) took over the operation of the Damang Mine, signs of a new relationship between the mining company and its host communities are beginning to emerge. The chiefs also claim that infrastructure works, local employment and structured community engagement taking centre stage. They also argue that one can talk about the first earthworks for a proposed airstrip at the Huni waste dump to the commencement of work on the Damang-Subri road and preparations for three astroturf facilities adding that “a number of commitments announced at the transition of the mine are already moving into implementation.” At the same time, nearly 400 people from the mine’s catchment communities have entered various stages of DGML’s recruitment process, with 180 already engaged and working and another 220 either progressing through recruitment or awaiting results. According to the chiefs, it is these developments that promted them to hold this press conference. They, however, say the early momentum must be sustained and translated into lasting improvements in livelihoods, infrastructure and local economic participation throughout the life of the mine. From Transition to Implementation The Damang mining lease transitioned to DGML on April 18, 2026, marking a significant change in the ownership and management of an operation that has been central to the economic life of the area for more than three decades. The transition created considerable expectations among host communities, particularly around employment, infrastructure, local business opportunities and their participation in decisions concerning the mine. Four months on, community leaders say some of those expectations are beginning to receive concrete responses. Airstrip Moves Beyond Announcement One of the most significant developments is the proposed airstrip at the Huni waste dump. DGML has confirmed that the facility has been designed and that initial earthworks have begun. The company has also brought the relevant regulatory and local authorities into the process. The Ghana Civil Aviation Authority and the Prestea-Huni Valley Municipal Assembly have been invited to the site to inspect the progress of the works. For the communities, the development is important because the proposed airstrip has moved beyond a project announcement to preliminary physical works and regulatory engagement. When completed, they believe the facility could improve connectivity, support the mine’s operations, attract investment and create new economic opportunities for businesses and residents in the wider area. The communities are therefore looking forward to the completion of the regulatory and technical processes required to take the project into full construction. Damang-Subri Road Gets Moving Road infrastructure is another area where the communities are seeing early activity. Work has commenced on the Damang-Subri section of the Damang-Subri-Praso-Cape Coast road. The road is regarded by residents as a critical link for the movement of people, goods and services and as an important connection between the mining communities and commercial centres beyond the immediate catchment. The communities believe improved road infrastructure could reduce transportation difficulties, improve access to markets, schools and health facilities and support businesses operating in the area. They are therefore calling for sustained collaboration between DGML, the Government and relevant agencies to ensure that the road improvement efforts translate into a durable solution to the longstanding challenges along the corridor. The development of sports infrastructure , is another thing that the chiefs highlighted in their engagement. DGML has indicated that the contractor is expected to mobilise a team and commence work by the middle of August. For the youth, the proposed parks represent more than recreational facilities. Community leaders believe they could provide platforms for football development, talent identification, youth engagement and community activities while giving young people access to better sporting infrastructure. The communities are consequently looking forward to seeing the projects move from site assessment and preparatory activities to actual construction. 400 locals in Employment Pipeline Perhaps the most immediate benefit being felt by residents is employment. DGML has reached an agreement with its host communities under which 60 per cent of its employees are expected to come from the local communities, with the remaining 40 per cent sourced externally, including employees’ wards, corporate sources and Ghana at large. Nearly 400 locals have already entered various stages of the recruitment process. Of these, 180 candidates have been engaged and are currently working. Another 135 candidates selected for positions including maintenance, heavy-duty driving, security and general hands are progressing through the final stages of recruitment, including pre-employment medical examinations and induction. A further 85 candidates have completed interviews and are awaiting their results. The communities regard the numbers as an important early indication that local people can secure a meaningful share of the economic opportunities generated by the mine.

items.title: OQTF annulée : la brillante étudiante en médecine obtient son titre de séjour
items.description: Tout est bien qui finit bien pour la brillante étudiante algérienne en médecine qui faisait l’objet d’une procédure d’expulsion en France. Rania Ameur (23 ans), étudiante algérienne en médecine à l'université de Lille, menacée d’expulsion depuis le 4 août dernier, peut enfin pousser un ouf de soulagement. L’OQTF (Obligation de Quitter le Territoire Français) qui pendait, comme une épée de Damoclès, au-dessus de sa tête, n’est plus qu’un mauvais souvenir puisqu’elle vient d’obtenir un titre de séjour l’autorisant à poursuivre ses études tranquillement, en quatrième année de cardiologie, dès septembre prochain. D’OQTF à titre de séjour : une brillante étudiante algérienne en médecine évite l’expulsion Un titre de séjour, renouvelable à chaque nouvelle année universitaire, a finalement tranché le préfet du Nord, suite à la pétition lancée en ligne, à l’initiative de Patrice Vergriete, ancien ministre et président de la communauté urbaine de Dunkerque, et de Régis Bordet, le président de l’Université de Lille et qui a recueilli plus de 15 000 signatures. Une « aberration totale » avait également commenté Bernard Champagne, président de la Ligue des droits de l’Homme de Dunkerque, qui a apporté son soutien inconditionnel à la jeune étudiante algérienne. L’OQTF avait ébranlé Rania. Elle avait interprété cette décision administrative « comme une grande violence, une humiliation même » comme l'a rapporté le quotidien L a Voix du Nord . La jeune femme, qui a posé ses valises, à Dunkerque, avec ses parents, à l’âge de 15 ans, rappelle qu’elle est rentrée en France légalement, avec un visa et non en traversant la Méditerranée à la nage. Un parcours sans faute Rania Ameur a toujours été une élève assidue. Après avoir décroché son bac avec mention dans un lycée privé à Dunkerque, elle se lance avec brio dans une licence de psychologie. L’étudiante ne s’arrête pas en si bon chemin et passe le concours d’entrée en médecine. Classée 96e sur 1000 étudiants, elle rejoint les bancs de l’université de médecine à Lille et endosse, dans la foulée, le costume de présidente des étudiants de ce campus. Déterminée à aller au bout de ses rêves, la brillante étudiante obtient une « bourse d’engagement » de la Communauté urbaine de Dunkerque. Un mécanisme mis en place pour lutter contre la désertification des hôpitaux. Contre rétribution, le futur médecin s’engage à exercer son métier, pendant au moins cinq ans, dans le Dunkerquois. Dans trois semaines, l’étudiante commencera son stage d’externe en médecine au CHU, qui lui permettra de poursuivre sereinement ses études de cardiologie et de contribuer à pallier le manque de médecins spécialistes dans la région. L’article OQTF annulée : la brillante étudiante en médecine obtient son titre de séjour est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: How to apply: Nigerian Army opens portal for Short Service Combatant Commission
items.description: The Nigerian Army has opened its recruitment portal for eligible Nigerians seeking to join the force as officers under the Short Service Combatant Commission (SSCC) Course 50/2027. The recruitment exercise is open to qualified civilians and serving military personnel who meet the stipulated requirements for the commission. Successful applicants who complete the required training and are commissioned will serve in the Nigerian Army’s Combat Arms, including the Infantry and Armour Corps, as well as Combat Support Arms such as the Artillery, Engineers, Signals and Intelligence Corps. How to apply Interested and eligible applicants are required to visit the official Nigerian Army recruitment portal to begin the application process. Applicants should: Visit the Nigerian Army’s official recruitment portal. Select the SSCC option. Carefully read and follow the application instructions provided on the portal. Complete and submit the application as required. Application deadline The deadline for applications is Saturday, October 17, 2026. The Nigerian Army urged prospective applicants and members of the public to be cautious of fraudulent recruitment announcements and websites. The Army specifically advised the public to disregard any online application portal or recruitment announcement claiming to have opened before the official publication. Applicants were also advised to rely only on information released through official Nigerian Army channels. The Army said prospective applicants and members of the public should also look out for official recruitment jingles on television and radio stations following the publication. items.title: Cheddar’s application thrown out, High Court awards GH¢20,000 costs against him in Cola Holdings case
items.description: The High Court in Accra has dismissed an application by businessman Nana Kwame Bediako (alias Cheddar) seeking to restrain the enforcement of a $14.9 million judgment obtained by UK-based Cola Holdings Limited, awarding costs of GH¢20,000 against him. The application, filed by lawyer Bobby Banson, sought to prevent Cola Holdings from enforcing the English High Court judgment against Mr Bediako personally pending the determination of an appeal against the refusal to set aside registration of the judgment in Ghana. Justice Doris Awuah Dabanka-Bekoe of the Commercial Division dismissed the application on July 27, 2026. The judgment, dated January 23, 2025, was obtained by Cola Holdings against Nana Kwame Bediako personally and registered in Ghana on May 20, 2025. An earlier attempt by Bediako’s lawyers to set aside the registration was refused by the court on November 27, 2025. The English court ordered Bediako to pay $14,928,314.70, plus interest at eight per cent per annum, amounting to $3,271.96 per day from January 23, 2025. At the Treasury exchange rate of GH₵16.15 to the dollar, the total amount, including interest and costs, is estimated at approximately GH₵258.76 million. Background to the dispute The judgment stems from a Deed of Indemnity Bediako signed in respect of his share of the repayment of a loan from the International Finance Corporation. Cola Holdings guaranteed the loan to Kensington Residential Partners 1 Ltd, a company in which Mr Bediako and Azad Cola hold shares. Following default, IFC called on Cola Holdings as guarantor to settle the loan, which Cola Holdings did. IFC then assigned its interest in the loan to Cola Holdings. Cola Holdings sought unsuccessfully to have Mr Bediako fulfil his obligation to repay his share of the loan before instituting proceedings in the High Court in London. Mr Bediako has maintained that the dispute stems from a corporate loan rather than a personal one and has argued that the judgment was obtained improperly. Court’s ruling In dismissing the application, Justice Dabanka-Bekoe applied the principles governing stays of execution pending appeal, as established in Joseph v Jebeille and affirmed by the Supreme Court in NDK Financial Services Ltd v Yiadom Construction and Electrical Works Ltd. The court found that Mr Bediako’s grounds of appeal, including arguments about the currency of the debt, the interest rate applied, and alleged public policy violations, did not establish arguable points of substance sufficient to warrant injunctive relief. Assets within the jurisdiction Central to the court’s decision was the finding that Cola Holdings holds identifiable assets within Ghana. The court noted that the Respondent exhibited a certificate of registration of a mortgage from the Registrar of Companies and a memorandum of registration of mortgage at the Lands Commission, demonstrating registered security interests in immovable and other assets in Ghana. These same documents were exhibited by Mr Bediako himself in his earlier application to set aside the registration. The court rejected Mr Bediako’s assertion that Cola Holdings had “no traceable assets in Ghana,” describing the claim as “demonstrably at odds with the record”. Costs awarded The court awarded costs of GH₵20,000 against Mr Bediako. The judge declined to award punitive costs, noting that a litigant is entitled to test a ruling by appeal and seek protection pending that appeal. The ruling follows a separate High Court decision on July 21, 2026, which granted Cola Holdings and its Receiver police assistance to take possession of the No. 1 Oxford Street Hotel in Osu, a property linked to Mr Bediako. The court in that matter found that Cola Holdings had properly registered its security interest over the property and was entitled to enforce its rights under the Borrowers and Lenders Act, 2020 (Act 1052). Cola Holdings and the Receiver were represented in the injunction application by Tsatsu Tsikata and Tata Kosi Foliba, while Mr Bediako was represented by Bobby Banson.

items.title: Adu-Boahene, wife may cross-examine prosecution witness themselves if lawyers stay away, Judge warns
items.description: The High Court in Accra has technically given former Director-General of the National Signals Bureau (NSB), Kwabena Adu-Boahene, and his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, six days to secure the presence of their lawyers for the continuation of their trial on August 17. The court warned that if they fail to appear with counsel on the next adjourned date, they will be required to personally continue the cross-examination of the fourth prosecution witness. Justice Francis Apangabonu Achibonga, a Justice of the Court of Appeal sitting as an additional High Court judge, further directed that if the accused persons fail to conduct the cross-examination themselves, the witness will be discharged. The directive followed proceedings on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, when Adu-Boahene and his wife appeared in court without their legal team. The prosecution was led by Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai, together with Chief State Attorney Sarah Fafa Kpodo, Principal State Attorney Esi Dentaa Yankah and EOCO Assistant Staff Officer Rabiatu Abdulai. Defence lawyers led by Samuel Atta Akyea were absent, although the matter had been scheduled for the continuation of the further cross-examination of the fourth prosecution witness. The defence team had earlier written to the Chief Justice indicating that they would not be available to participate in proceedings during the legal vacation. Adu-Boahene asks court for time Addressing the court, Adu-Boahene asked for an opportunity to reach his lawyers and clarify their position. “It’s been quite a challenge reaching him this morning,” he said, referring to Mr Atta Akyea. “As recently as this past weekend, I am aware that a few of them have been included in script marking outside Accra. For the lead counsel [Atta Akyea], I am not sure if he is even in the jurisdiction,” he added. He therefore appealed to the court to give them time to resolve the issue. “If you will kindly indulge us, we will try to resolve the issue with them,” he said. Deputy AG: Lawyers cannot decide whether court sits Dr Srem-Sai opposed any suggestion that proceedings could not continue merely because counsel had decided not to attend during the legal vacation. “We are aware, and I have spoken to counsel who was categorical that he had written a letter to the Chief Justice, this court’s registrar, and the Ghana Bar Association that he would exercise his alleged right to not attend court proceedings during the vacation,” he told the court. According to the Deputy Attorney-General, the power to determine whether proceedings may be held during the legal vacation rests with the Chief Justice, subject to the trial judge’s authority to control proceedings. “We are not aware of any law, rule, practice, or convention which allows a lawyer or a group of lawyers for that matter to decide whether there should be proceedings in court or not,” he submitted. He said where a lawyer has a genuine reason for seeking an adjournment, the appropriate course is to make an application to the court. “If a lawyer has a genuine reason to absent himself from court or to have the proceedings adjourned, what we know at the Bar is that the lawyer would make a prayer to the court for the court to grant such accommodation on a case-by-case basis,” he said. He added that it remained the judge’s responsibility to determine whether proceedings should continue. “Whatever case it may be, it remains the province of the judge alone to determine whether there should be proceedings, having obtained a warrant to sit during the vacation,” he said. Read Also: Selective justice claims false, lawyers only trying to delay cases — Deputy AG Court grants final opportunity In his ruling, Justice Achibonga said the accused persons deserved an opportunity to put their house in order regarding legal representation. The judge noted that counsel for the accused persons had been present when the case was adjourned to August 11 through to August 13, yet failed to appear. “Counsel for the accused persons was present when the suit was adjourned to today [August 11] through to 13 August 2026, yet counsel is absent without any reason,” the court said. Justice Achibonga acknowledged the letter written by defence counsel to the Chief Justice on August 5 seeking reconsideration of the directive to sit during the legal vacation, as well as the Ghana Bar Association’s August 10 letter raising similar concerns. However, he stressed that those letters did not amount to a stay of proceedings. “All I can do as a trial judge is to take note of the said letters, as the same do not amount to a stay of proceedings in this suit,” he said. “Having been issued a warrant by the Chief Justice to sit during the legal vacation and to conduct hearings, until the said warrant is revoked, I am mandated to continue to sit as a vacation judge and conduct hearings.” The judge, however, said it would be unfair to require the accused persons to immediately take over the cross-examination without giving them an opportunity to resolve the issue of legal representation. “The question to ask is, would it be fair to the accused persons if I decided to proceed today and asked them to continue with the cross-examination of PW4? I do not think so,” he said. “In my view, even if counsel had abandoned their clients, it is only fair and proper to give the client an opportunity to advise himself or herself so as to enable court business to continue undistracted.” He therefore adjourned the matter to August 17. “If by the next date [August 17] the accused are not represented by counsel, they shall be made to cross-examine the witness themselves, failing which PW4 would be discharged,” the court directed. Adu-Boahene, Angela Adjei Boateng and Advantage Solutions are facing 11 charges, including allegations of stealing GH¢49.1 million intended for a cyber security defence system. They have pleaded not guilty and are on bail.

items.title: Investigate alleged US$1.7bn loss in connection with Gold Purchase Programme – Abena Osei Asare to Mahama
items.description: The Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC)and Member of Parliament for Atiwa East, Abena Osei-Asare, has called on President John Dramani Mahama to order a comprehensive investigation into the alleged US$1.7 billion loss associated with the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP). Speaking at a press briefing on matters concerning GoldBod, the Bank of Ghana (BoG) and the funded foreign exchange forward sale programme, the MP said the scale of reported losses associated with the domestic gold purchase programme warranted further scrutiny. Osei-Asare said she was particularly concerned about the disparity between figures reported by the Bank of Ghana and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) regarding losses under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. According to her, the IMF’s latest Article IV consultation estimated losses from the programme at about US$1.7 billion, while the Bank of Ghana’s 2025 financial statements reported a loss of US$214 million. She questioned how the significant difference between the two figures was accounted for and called for greater transparency. “The IMF comes, and the IMF is privy to all the data and everything, and says no, the loss is not $214 million as you recorded, but $1.7 billion,” she said. Osei-Asare also called on the accounting firm that audited the Bank of Ghana’s financial statements to explain how the approximately US$1.4 billion difference was treated. “I’m asking the accounting firm that audited Bank of Ghana, I want to hear from them on this. So how did they treat the difference of close to $1.4 billion?” she questioned. The Atiwa East MP said the reported US$1.7 billion loss was equivalent to approximately GH¢22 billion, describing the amount as significant given Ghana’s competing development needs. She compared the figure with the reported financial requirement of the Ministry of Health to recruit nurses, arguing that a fraction of the amount could have been used to create jobs for unemployed health professionals. “The Minister of Health is complaining about the fact that he needs GH¢6 billion to recruit nurses. And here we are, GH¢22 billion is going down the drain,” she said. According to Osei-Asare, investing GH¢6 billion in the recruitment exercise could help employ more than 10,000 nurses, reduce unemployment and generate additional revenue for the state through income taxes. The MP further questioned GoldBod’s reported profit of about GH¢909 million , arguing that the figure should be assessed alongside the reported losses incurred under the broader gold purchase arrangements. She also questioned the discounts reportedly granted to gold off-takers, saying the public deserved an explanation for the financial implications of such arrangements. Osei-Asare stressed that her concerns were not intended to attack GoldBod but to ensure transparency and accountability in the management of public funds. “This is not about GoldBod coming out with insults. We want them to elevate their discussion. Tell us their side of the story,” she said. She maintained that the reported figures and financial arrangements surrounding GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana required further investigation to establish the facts and safeguard public resources.

items.title: Solar eclipse sparks scramble for protective glasses across Europe
items.description: The scramble for protective glasses has reached fever pitch across Europe ahead of Wednesday’s rare total solar eclipse, as pharmacies, opticians and other shops struggled to keep them in stock. In Spain, where parts of the country will be in the path of totality, finding certified protective glasses has become increasingly difficult, with many distribution points reporting they have run out. A notice posted at the entrance of Madrid’s National Museum of Natural Sciences said its supply of protective glasses was exhausted. The museum was among 30 science institutions across the country taking part in a campaign organised by the government to distribute two million pairs of glasses for free. Some pharmacies in central Madrid still had supplies Tuesday, generally selling certified glasses for safely viewing the Sun for between three and four euros ($4.60) a pair. But Carles Sisquella, who runs an optical shop in Barcelona, said his store had been out of stock for 10 days. “There are now a lot of people who obviously won’t be able to get glasses,” he said. Doctors warn that looking directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse can damage the retina, potentially harming the cells responsible for sharp central vision. “I’ve been asking around since Friday, but they’re nowhere to be found,” a woman named Mabel told AFP in Barcelona after another fruitless search. French supermarket chain Carrefour’s Spanish unit said demand for eclipse glasses has “grown exponentially”, increasing twentyfold in recent days compared with the same period last month. ‘Gone in 30 minutes’ The rush is being repeated across Europe. In Brussels, where about 90 percent of the Sun will be covered by the Moon, people were also racing to find glasses. With a seeming majority of opticians and pharmacists out of stock, pastry chef Arno Dossogne, 37, struck gold at a small opticians’ store that received a last-minute shipment Monday afternoon. “I got some for me, my boyfriend and a couple of friends whose online order got cancelled!” he told AFP. “It was this or nothing. You can’t mess around, or you’ll burn your eyes.” The opticians’ manager Fouad Mehdaoui told AFP he acted on a tip from his pharmacist wife, placing large orders of glasses early on, but even then was outrun by demand and had to order more. “Two boxes just came in with 100 pairs in total — they were gone in 30 minutes,” he told AFP as a stream of eclipse enthusiasts filed in the store, by chance or word of mouth, and an employee fielded non-stop phone enquiries. In France, where the eclipse will be partial, some pharmacies have been stripped of their supplies while others were still receiving shipments — and charging significantly more. Customers lined up outside La Pharmacie du Soleil in Paris on Monday afternoon to buy glasses for 5.95 euros a pair, only to be disappointed when staff displayed an empty box. ‘Pure madness’ The pharmacist asked customers to check back later, saying another shipment of 500 pairs was expected that evening. “Come back in an hour or tomorrow morning,” he told customers. “It’s pure madness.” Philippe Besset, president of France’s Federation of Pharmaceutical Trade Unions, said demand had been far greater than expected. A few months ago, suppliers had offered pharmacies around 200 pairs each, enough to equip about four million people, he told AFP. “But obviously more people want to watch the eclipse,” he said. Marine Tondelier, leader of France’s Greens, accused the government of failing to properly prepare for the eclipse, calling the struggle to secure glasses a “fiasco”. She contrasted it with the 1999 eclipse, when more than 30 million approved glasses were distributed nationwide. In Rome, Claudia Rinaldi of eyewear shop Vision Optika said a first batch of eclipse glasses “sold out almost immediately”. Her store was hoping to receive a second shipment by Wednesday morning, with customers already calling to ask about their availability. The shortage has prompted eye specialists to warn people against buying uncertified alternatives. In Spain, authorities on Monday withdrew six models from the market because of the risk of eye injuries. Vanguard News The post Solar eclipse sparks scramble for protective glasses across Europe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Political parties, judiciary need reforms to protect African democracy — Asiedu Nketiah
items.description: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has called for reforms within political parties and the judiciary to strengthen democratic governance and rebuild public trust across Africa. He said political parties and the judiciary have critical roles to play in protecting democracy but cautioned that neither institution could effectively perform that role without credibility, accountability, competence and public trust. Mr. Asiedu Nketiah made the remarks on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Democracy Dialogue in Bauchi, Nigeria, on the theme: “Beyond Elections: Can Political Parties and the Judiciary Save African Democracy?” Speaking on the panel on political parties and the judiciary, he argued that democracy should not be judged solely by the conduct of elections but also by how political authority is exercised between elections. “Elections determine who receives the authority to govern. They do not, by themselves, determine whether that authority will be exercised lawfully, whether constitutional limits will be respected, whether the opposition will remain legitimate or whether government will improve the lives of the people,” he said. Asiedu Nketiah cited Ghana’s democratic experience under the Fourth Republic as an example of democratic institutionalisation, noting that the country has conducted nine consecutive general elections since 1992. He highlighted the peaceful transfers of power recorded in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024 as evidence that governing parties in Africa can lose power and transfer authority peacefully through elections. He particularly referenced the 2008 presidential election, which was decided by less than half a percentage point, saying political leaders, institutions and citizens prevented the closely contested election from becoming a national crisis. He also cited former President John Dramani Mahama’s concession after the 2016 election and Vice-President Mahamudu Bawumia’s concession ahead of the formal declaration of the 2024 election results. According to him, such concessions should be viewed as important contributions to constitutional democracy rather than mere political courtesies. However, Asiedu Nketiah warned against complacency, pointing to election-related violence during the 2020 elections as a reminder that democratic gains could be reversed. The NDC National Chairman called for major reforms within political parties, insisting that they should not operate merely as electoral machines or vehicles for individual political ambitions. He said parties must strengthen internal democracy, tolerate legitimate dissent and create opportunities for women, young people, persons with disabilities and people without significant financial resources to participate meaningfully in politics. Mr. Asiedu Nketiah also identified the rising cost of political campaigns as a threat to internal party democracy. He argued that when political participation becomes heavily dependent on wealth, political parties risk selecting candidates based on their financial capacity rather than competence. He therefore called for measures to reduce financial barriers to political participation and strengthen party institutions responsible for policy development, research, civic education and leadership training. On women’s participation, he noted that women currently occupy 40 of Ghana’s 276 parliamentary seats, representing 14.5 per cent. He also called for practical pathways to increase youth participation in policy development, party leadership, Parliament and executive responsibilities. Mr. Asiedu Nketiah also stressed the importance of an independent and credible judiciary in resolving political disputes and protecting constitutional democracy. He referenced Ghana’s presidential election petitions following the 2012 and 2020 elections as examples of how political disagreements can be transferred from the streets to the courts. He said respect for judicial decisions does not prevent political actors from criticising judicial reasoning, noting that legitimate criticism is part of constitutional democracy, while intimidation and threats are unacceptable. However, he said judicial independence must be accompanied by transparency, consistency, ethical standards and public accountability. Citing public perceptions of Ghana’s judiciary, he said concerns about access to justice, affordability and delays could undermine confidence in the institution. “Judicial authority cannot depend only on constitutional text; it must also rest on citizens’ confidence that justice is accessible, impartial and timely,” he said. He urged African judiciaries to remain strong enough to restrain governments, protect opposition parties, defend fundamental rights and enforce constitutional limits. At the same time, he cautioned that courts should not become “alternative political chambers” or replace decisions that constitutionally belong to elected institutions and citizens. Mr. Asiedu Nketiah proposed enforceable standards for political parties covering internal democracy, campaign financing, audited accounts, candidate selection and leadership succession. He also called for transparent criteria for judicial appointments and promotions, timely publication of constitutional judgments, stronger legal aid and improved public access to information on court performance. He urged political parties, courts, electoral bodies, civil society organisations, the media and academia to engage in dialogue before political crises emerge. In his closing remarks, Mr. Asiedu Nketiah said African democracy would not be secured merely by holding more elections. “The future of African democracy will not be secured merely by conducting more elections. It will be secured by institutions that make elections meaningful, government accountable, constitutional limits effective and peaceful transfers of power normal,” he said. He stressed that political parties must recognise that political power is temporary and belongs ultimately to the people, while the judiciary must protect its independence through integrity and public confidence. According to him, when political parties respect constitutional limits, courts administer justice fairly, governments deliver development and citizens remain engaged beyond elections, democracy can evolve into a durable system of public trust, peaceful competition and accountable governance.

items.title: GAUA strike: NLC says administrators may have breached procedure for industrial action
items.description: The National Labour Commission (NLC) has raised concerns over the procedure followed by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) before embarking on its ongoing industrial action. According to JoyNews’ Stephen Mensah, sources at the Commission said, GAUA may not have complied with the legal requirements governing industrial action, particularly the obligation to notify both its employers and the NLC before commencing the strike. The concerns come as the university administrators push for action to address what they describe as disparities in allowances and other conditions of service. The NLC is reported to have indicated that GAUA failed to formally notify the Commission and the affected employers before withdrawing their services. Under Ghana’s Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651), parties involved in an industrial dispute are required to exhaust prescribed dispute-resolution procedures before resorting to industrial action. Section 159 of the Act provides for written notice to be given before industrial action is undertaken. The notice is intended to trigger a period during which the employer, the union or workers’ association, and the NLC can engage to resolve the dispute and avert industrial action. Sources at the NLC say the required notice is important because it gives the Commission an opportunity to intervene in the dispute before workers proceed with a strike. The development could therefore raise questions about the procedural validity of GAUA’s current industrial action, although the substantive concerns underlying the strike remain unresolved. GAUA has maintained that it was compelled to take action after what it considers prolonged disparities in allowances between university administrators and other categories of staff. The association has also argued that its concerns have not received the attention they deserve and that the strike is intended to compel the relevant authorities to address the disparities. Meanwhile, the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) has criticised the industrial action, describing the strike as unjustified. GNAT says it is seeking to ensure that the dispute is resolved as quickly as possible. The NLC’s intervention is expected to focus on both the procedural issues surrounding the strike and the underlying grievances raised by the administrators.

items.title: Houet : Claudine Sanou distinguée « Colombe de la Paix » aux Ambassadeurs Awards 2026
items.description: Houet : Claudine Sanou distinguée « Colombe de la Paix » aux Ambassadeurs Awards 2026 Bobo-Dioulasso, 11 août 2026 (AIB) – La collaboratrice de l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB) dans le Houet, Claudine Sanou, a été distinguée dans la catégorie « Colombe de la Paix » lors de la troisième édition des Ambassadeurs Awards, tenue le samedi 8 août 2026 à la Maison de la culture Monseigneur Anselme Titianma Sanon. Placée sous le thème « Solidarité et Résilience : Honorer ceux qui bâtissent l’espoir au cœur des défis », la cérémonie a récompensé des personnes, des organisations et entreprises qui contribuent au développement social, humanitaire, économique et durable du Burkina Faso. La catégorie féminine a notamment mis à l’honneur l’entrepreneuriat, le leadership et l’impact social féminins, ainsi que la « Colombe de la Paix ». Claudine Sanou s’est distinguée dans cette dernière catégorie pour son engagement en faveur de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et de la transformation positive des communautés à travers les médias et les réseaux sociaux. Ses contenus, axés notamment sur l’espoir, l’apaisement des cœurs et l’édification des communautés, ont retenu l’attention du jury. Recevant son trophée et son attestation, la lauréate a exprimé sa satisfaction et sa fierté, estimant que cette distinction constitue une source supplémentaire de motivation pour poursuivre son engagement. « C’est un sentiment d’immense joie et de fierté qui m’anime aujourd’hui. Mon cœur déborde de gratitude et les mots me manquent pour exprimer tout ce que je ressens en recevant ce trophée », a-t-elle déclaré, avant de remercier toutes les personnes qui l’ont soutenue. Selon le président du comité d’organisation, Elie Ali Traoré, « le Gala des Ambassadeurs Awards est un tremplin pour les acteurs du développement économique, social et humanitaire du Burkina Faso et d’ailleurs, parce que c’est un cadre qui réunit les jeunes qui ont un impact sur leurs communautés », a-t-il précisé.
